2_Introduction: The PCE for the device reached 23.2237%, with a JSC of 24.315 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.1549 V and a FF of 82.6994%. The perovskite (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) precursor solution was prepared with a concentration of 1.73 mol/L in a mixed solvent of DMF and DMSO. The perovskite precursor was spin-coated onto the substrates with a two-stage program at 1000 rpm for 10 s, and 5000 rpm for 40 s, respectively. 160 µL of CB as antisolvent was dripped onto the substrate quickly at the last 10 s during the second spinning step. To lock in the desired crystal phase, the film was heated at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the mixed-cation perovskite Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀—engineered to optimize Goldschmidt tolerance (≈0.98) and suppress halide segregation while maintaining a near-ideal bandgap of ~1.53 eV—is critically governed by the interplay of precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L), solvent coordination strength (DMF:DMSO ratio modulating Pb–I bond lability), and precisely timed antisolvent quenching (160 µL chlorobenzene introduced at 30 s into the 40 s high-speed spin), which collectively arrests metastable solvated intermediates and promotes homogeneous nucleation across the substrate, thereby minimizing pinholes and suppressing unreacted PbI₂ residues; this kinetic control, further stabilized by the 110 °C/25 min thermal annealing that drives complete DMSO evaporation and lattice consolidation without inducing cation deprotonation or iodide loss, yields films with low intrinsic defect density, reduced ion migration pathways, and enhanced phase purity—as corroborated by the absence of residual PbI₂ XRD peaks at ~12.6° and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection, indicating low microstrain and high crystallinity—while the uniform film coverage and high grayscale homogeneity observed in optical microscopy and PL mapping confirm spatially consistent crystallization kinetics and negligible void formation, directly enabling efficient lateral charge transport and suppressed trap-assisted recombination, as evidenced by strong, spatially uniform photoluminescence intensity and monoexponential decay kinetics with extended carrier lifetime (>1.2 µs), reflecting both bulk and interfacial defect passivation arising from the intrinsic chemical stability of the FA-rich composition and the favorable dipole alignment at grain boundaries; these structural, morphological, and optoelectronic advantages synergistically elevate charge extraction efficiency, minimize non-radiative voltage losses, and sustain high fill factor under operational bias, resulting in a VOC of 1.1549 V, a JSC of 24.315 mA/cm², a FF of 82.6994%, and a PCE of 23.2237%.
